subproblem.title: Sup and Lipschitz bounds for convolution with a bounded Lipschitz kernel (step A1(ii), T1)
subproblem.statement: For every n ∈ ℕ, all ρ, F : ℝⁿ → ℝ, every real A and every K ∈ ℝ≥0 such that |ρ(x)| ≤ A for all x, ρ is K-Lipschitz and F is Lebesgue integrable on ℝⁿ, the convolution (ρ⋆F)(x) := convolution ρ F (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume x = ∫ ρ(t)F(x − t) dt satisfies, for all x, y ∈ ℝⁿ: |(ρ⋆F)(x)| ≤ A·∫|F| and |(ρ⋆F)(x) − (ρ⋆F)(y)| ≤ K·‖x − y‖·∫|F|.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (ρ F : Rn n → ℝ) (A : ℝ) (K : ℝ≥0), (∀ x, |ρ x| ≤ A) → LipschitzWith K ρ → Integrable F volume → ∀ x y : Rn n, |convolution ρ F (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume x| ≤ A * (∫ t, |F t|) ∧ |convolution ρ F (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume x - convolution ρ F (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume y| ≤ K * ‖x - y‖ * (∫ t, |F t|)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, Theorem 2.6 (p. 50). The printed proof reduces compactness to precompactness in L¹_loc(U), proved “involving mollification and Arzela's theorem” [GT01, Thm 7.22]; this step supplies the uniform bounds that make the mollified sequence equibounded and equi-Lipschitz. The argument below is step A1(ii) (T1) of the reviewed proof supplied to node root.bv_results-a1.compactness-a1 (Section A of the parent root.bv_results-a1), specialized to this self-contained statement with the details filled in. Notation: ℝⁿ = Rn n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μ = volume (Lebesgue measure), ∫⁻ is the lower Lebesgue integral in [0,∞], ‖a‖ₑ ∈ [0,∞) the extended norm, ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal.

Statement recalled. ρ, F : ℝⁿ → ℝ, A ∈ ℝ with |ρ(x)| ≤ A for all x, K ∈ ℝ≥0 with ρ K-Lipschitz, and F ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ). The convolution is (ρ⋆F)(x) := convolution ρ F (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume x = ∫ ρ(t) F(x − t) dt (lsmul a b = a · b). Claim, for all x, y: |(ρ⋆F)(x)| ≤ A ∫|F| and |(ρ⋆F)(x) − (ρ⋆F)(y)| ≤ K ‖x − y‖ ∫|F|.

1. ρ is continuous (a Lipschitz map), hence measurable; and A ≥ |ρ(0)| ≥ 0.

2. Swapped form. Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ is invariant under translations and under x ↦ −x, so the substitution t ↦ z − t gives, for every z, (ρ⋆F)(z) = ∫ ρ(z − t) F(t) dt (Mathlib convolution_lsmul_swap; smul on ℝ is multiplication).

3. Integrability. For every z, the function t ↦ ρ(z − t) F(t) is integrable: F is integrable and t ↦ ρ(z − t) is continuous (hence a.e.-strongly measurable) with |ρ(z − t)| ≤ A for all t (Integrable.bdd_mul).

4. Sup bound. By step 2, |(ρ⋆F)(x)| = |∫ ρ(x − t) F(t) dt| ≤ ∫ A |F(t)| dt = A ∫ |F|, using norm_integral_le_of_norm_le with the integrable majorant t ↦ A|F(t)| (pointwise |ρ(x − t) F(t)| = |ρ(x − t)| |F(t)| ≤ A |F(t)|) and integral_const_mul.

5. Lipschitz bound. By steps 2 and 3 and linearity of the integral (integral_sub), (ρ⋆F)(x) − (ρ⋆F)(y) = ∫ (ρ(x − t) − ρ(y − t)) F(t) dt. For every t, |ρ(x − t) − ρ(y − t)| ≤ K ‖(x − t) − (y − t)‖ = K ‖x − y‖ (LipschitzWith.dist_le_mul), so the integrand has absolute value ≤ K ‖x − y‖ |F(t)|, an integrable majorant. Hence (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le, integral_const_mul) |(ρ⋆F)(x) − (ρ⋆F)(y)| ≤ ∫ K ‖x − y‖ |F(t)| dt = K ‖x − y‖ ∫ |F|. ∎
proof_key_steps: Swap: (ρ⋆F)(z) = ∫ ρ(z − t)F(t) dt (convolution_lsmul_swap; Lebesgue measure is translation and reflection invariant).
t ↦ ρ(z − t)F(t) is integrable (bounded continuous times integrable).
(ρ⋆F)(x) − (ρ⋆F)(y) = ∫(ρ(x − t) − ρ(y − t))F(t)dt with |ρ(x − t) − ρ(y − t)| ≤ K‖x − y‖, giving K‖x − y‖∫|F|.

audit.reason: The type exactly expresses both stated estimates with scalar multiplication and K coerced to a real. The proof justifies the swapped convolution formula, integrability of each product, subtraction of integrals, and the two integrable majorants. No compact-support assumption is needed.

subproblem.title: Finite L¹ nets on every compact subset give an L¹_loc-convergent subsequence (step A2, diagonal extraction)
subproblem.statement: For every n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝⁿ and every sequence u_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) of functions locally integrable on U such that for every compact Q ⊆ U and every ε > 0 there is a finite set F ⊆ ℕ with: every k has some j ∈ F with ∫⁻_Q ‖u_k(x) − u_j(x)‖ₑ dx < ofReal ε, there exist a strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ and v : ℝⁿ → ℝ such that v is locally integrable on U and u_{ψ(k)} → v in L¹_loc(U), i.e. ∫⁻_K ‖u_{ψ(k)} − v‖ₑ → 0 for every compact K ⊆ U (SimonGMT Chapter02.TendstoLocallyInL1On (fun k ↦ u (ψ k)) v U atTop).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Set (Rn n)) (u : ℕ → Rn n → ℝ), IsOpen U → (∀ k, LocallyIntegrableOn (u k) U volume) → (∀ Q : Set (Rn n), IsCompact Q → Q ⊆ U → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ F : Finset ℕ, ∀ k, ∃ j ∈ F, (∫⁻ x in Q, ‖u k x - u j x‖ₑ) < ENNReal.ofReal ε) → ∃ (ψ : ℕ → ℕ) (v : Rn n → ℝ), StrictMono ψ ∧ LocallyIntegrableOn v U volume ∧ Chapter02.TendstoLocallyInL1On (fun k ↦ u (ψ k)) v U atTop
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, Theorem 2.6 (p. 50). The printed proof reduces the claim to precompactness in L¹_loc(U); this step turns precompactness on every compact subset into an L¹_loc-convergent subsequence by compact exhaustion and diagonal extraction. The argument below is step A2 of the reviewed proof supplied to node root.bv_results-a1.compactness-a1 (Section A of the parent root.bv_results-a1), specialized to this self-contained statement with the details filled in. Notation: ℝⁿ = Rn n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μ = volume (Lebesgue measure), ∫⁻ is the lower Lebesgue integral in [0,∞], ‖a‖ₑ ∈ [0,∞) the extended norm, ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal.

Statement recalled. U ⊆ ℝⁿ is open, every u_k is locally integrable on U, and (finite-net hypothesis) for every compact Q ⊆ U and every ε > 0 there is a finite F ⊆ ℕ such that every k has some j ∈ F with ∫⁻_Q ‖u_k − u_j‖ₑ < ofReal ε. Claim: there are a strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ and v : ℝⁿ → ℝ with v locally integrable on U and, for every compact K ⊆ U, ∫⁻_K ‖u_{ψ(k)} − v‖ₑ → 0 as k → ∞ (Chapter02.TendstoLocallyInL1On (fun k ↦ u (ψ k)) v U atTop).

0. L¹ spaces. For a measurable Q let L¹(Q) := Lp ℝ 1 (μ.restrict Q); it is a complete metric space (Lp.instCompleteSpace). If f is integrable on Q, write [f]_Q := MemLp.toLp f ∈ L¹(Q) (memLp_one_iff_integrable). For f, g integrable on Q, edist([f]_Q, [g]_Q) = eLpNorm(f − g, 1, μ.restrict Q) = ∫⁻_Q ‖f − g‖ₑ (Lp.edist_toLp_toLp, eLpNorm_one_eq_lintegral_enorm); consequently dist([f]_Q, [g]_Q) < ε whenever ∫⁻_Q ‖f − g‖ₑ < ofReal ε (ENNReal.toReal_lt_of_lt_ofReal). Every element g of L¹(Q) has a strongly measurable representative ⇑g (Lp.stronglyMeasurable) which is integrable on Q, with [⇑g]_Q = g.

1. Compact exhaustion. For j ∈ ℕ let Q_j := {x ∈ closedBall(0, j + 1) : ofReal(1/(j + 1)) ≤ infEDist(x, Uᶜ)} (Metric.infEDist; if Uᶜ = ∅ then infEDist(x, ∅) = ∞ and Q_j = closedBall(0, j + 1), so no case distinction is needed; if U = ∅ every Q_j is empty and everything below holds trivially).
 (a) Q_j is compact: it is closed (closedBall is closed and x ↦ infEDist(x, Uᶜ) is continuous, so the superlevel set is closed) and bounded in the proper space ℝⁿ.
 (b) Q_j ⊆ U: if x ∉ U then x ∈ Uᶜ, so infEDist(x, Uᶜ) = 0 < ofReal(1/(j + 1)).
 (c) Q_j ⊆ interior Q_{j+1}: for x ∈ Q_j the set O := {y : ‖y‖ < j + 2 ∧ ofReal(1/(j + 2)) < infEDist(y, Uᶜ)} is open (continuity), contains x (‖x‖ ≤ j + 1 < j + 2 and infEDist(x, Uᶜ) ≥ 1/(j + 1) > 1/(j + 2)) and is contained in Q_{j+1}. In particular Q_j ⊆ Q_{j+1}, so i ≤ j implies Q_i ⊆ Q_j.
 (d) Every x ∈ U lies in some Q_j: Uᶜ is closed and x ∉ Uᶜ = closure Uᶜ, so infEDist(x, Uᶜ) > 0 (Metric.mem_closure_iff_infEDist_zero), and for j large ‖x‖ ≤ j + 1 and 1/(j + 1) ≤ infEDist(x, Uᶜ).
 (e) Every compact K ⊆ U lies in some Q_j: by (c) and (d) the increasing open sets interior Q_{j+1} (j ∈ ℕ) cover K; a finite subcover exists by compactness and, the sets being increasing, K ⊆ interior Q_{J+1} ⊆ Q_{J+1} for some J (IsCompact.elim_directed_cover).

2. Total boundedness. Fix j. Each u_k is integrable on Q_j (LocallyIntegrableOn.integrableOn_compact_subset with (a), (b)). Put f_{j,k} := [u_k]_{Q_j} ∈ L¹(Q_j) and S_j := {f_{j,k} : k ∈ ℕ}. S_j is totally bounded (Metric.totallyBounded_iff): given ε > 0, the finite-net hypothesis for Q = Q_j gives a finite F with S_j ⊆ ⋃_{i ∈ F} ball(f_{j,i}, ε) by step 0. Hence closure S_j is totally bounded (TotallyBounded.closure) and closed in the complete space L¹(Q_j), so it is compact (TotallyBounded.isCompact_of_isClosed).

3. Nested subsequences. In a metric space every sequence in a compact set has a subsequence converging to a point of that set (IsCompact.tendsto_subseq). Define recursively strictly increasing maps ψ_j : ℕ → ℕ and elements g_j ∈ L¹(Q_j): choose ψ_0 strictly increasing with f_{0,ψ_0(k)} → g_0 in L¹(Q_0) (the sequence lies in S_0 ⊆ closure S_0); given ψ_j, the sequence k ↦ f_{j+1,ψ_j(k)} lies in S_{j+1} ⊆ closure S_{j+1}, so choose φ_{j+1} strictly increasing and g_{j+1} with f_{j+1,ψ_j(φ_{j+1}(k))} → g_{j+1}, and put ψ_{j+1} := ψ_j ∘ φ_{j+1}. Since a subsequence of a convergent sequence converges to the same limit, for i ≤ j the sequence k ↦ f_{i,ψ_j(k)} also converges to g_i (ψ_j = ψ_i ∘ φ_{i+1} ∘ ⋯ ∘ φ_j).

4. Diagonal. Put ψ(k) := ψ_k(k). A strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ satisfies φ(m) ≥ m (StrictMono.id_le), so ψ(k + 1) = ψ_k(φ_{k+1}(k + 1)) ≥ ψ_k(k + 1) > ψ_k(k) = ψ(k); hence ψ is strictly increasing. Fix j. For k ≥ j, ψ_k = ψ_j ∘ χ_k with χ_k := φ_{j+1} ∘ ⋯ ∘ φ_k, so ψ(k) = ψ_j(m(k)) with m(k) := χ_k(k). Since ψ and ψ_j are strictly increasing, m is strictly increasing on {k ≥ j}, so m(k) → ∞, and therefore f_{j,ψ(k)} = f_{j,ψ_j(m(k))} → g_j in L¹(Q_j) as k → ∞. Let G_j := ⇑g_j (step 0). By step 0, e_j(k) := ∫⁻_{Q_j} ‖u_{ψ(k)} − G_j‖ₑ = edist(f_{j,ψ(k)}, g_j) → 0 (tendsto_iff_edist_tendsto_0).
 (Equivalent shortcut, convenient in Lean: the sequence k ↦ (f_{j,k})_{j∈ℕ} lies in ∏_j closure S_j, which is compact by Tychonoff (isCompact_univ_pi) and first countable as a countable product of metric spaces; IsCompact.tendsto_subseq gives one strictly increasing ψ along which every coordinate converges (tendsto_pi_nhds), which is exactly the conclusion of steps 3–4.)

5. Compatibility of the limits. Let i ≤ j, so Q_i ⊆ Q_j. All of u_{ψ(k)}, G_i, G_j are a.e.-strongly measurable on Q_i. By the triangle inequality for ‖·‖ₑ, additivity of ∫⁻ for a.e.-measurable summands and lintegral_mono_set,
   ∫⁻_{Q_i} ‖G_i − G_j‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_{Q_i} ‖G_i − u_{ψ(k)}‖ₑ + ∫⁻_{Q_i} ‖u_{ψ(k)} − G_j‖ₑ ≤ e_i(k) + e_j(k)
   for every k; the right side tends to 0, so ∫⁻_{Q_i} ‖G_i − G_j‖ₑ = 0, and therefore G_i = G_j μ-a.e. on Q_i (lintegral_eq_zero_iff').

6. Gluing. For x ∈ U let j(x) be the least j with x ∈ Q_j (it exists by 1(d)) and put v(x) := G_{j(x)}(x); for x ∉ U put v(x) := 0. Claim: for every j, v = G_j μ-a.e. on Q_j. Indeed Q_j is the finite union over i ≤ j of D_i := {x ∈ Q_j : j(x) = i} ⊆ Q_i (Q_j ⊆ U by 1(b)); on D_i we have v = G_i, and G_i = G_j a.e. on Q_i ⊇ D_i by step 5; a finite union of null sets is null.

7. Convergence. By step 6 and lintegral_congr_ae (for μ.restrict Q_j), ∫⁻_{Q_j} ‖u_{ψ(k)} − v‖ₑ = e_j(k) → 0 for every j. If K ⊆ U is compact, then K ⊆ Q_j for some j (1(e)), so 0 ≤ ∫⁻_K ‖u_{ψ(k)} − v‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_{Q_j} ‖u_{ψ(k)} − v‖ₑ (lintegral_mono_set), and the squeeze theorem gives ∫⁻_K ‖u_{ψ(k)} − v‖ₑ → 0. This is Chapter02.TendstoLocallyInL1On (fun k ↦ u (ψ k)) v U atTop.

8. Local integrability. For every j, G_j is integrable on Q_j and v = G_j a.e. on Q_j (step 6), so v is integrable on Q_j (Integrable.congr). Every compact K ⊆ U lies in some Q_j (1(e)), so v is integrable on K. Since U is open, hence locally closed (hU.isLocallyClosed), and ℝⁿ is locally compact, locallyIntegrableOn_iff gives LocallyIntegrableOn v U volume.

9. ψ is strictly increasing (step 4); together with steps 7 and 8 this proves the claim. ∎

The finite nets make {[u_k]_{Q_j}} totally bounded in the complete space L¹(Q_j), so its closure is compact.

subproblem.title: L¹(Q) approximation, uniform in k, by equibounded equi-Lipschitz functions gives finite L¹(Q) nets (step A1(iii)–(iv), elementary Arzelà–Ascoli)
subproblem.statement: For every n ∈ ℕ, every compact Q ⊆ ℝⁿ and every sequence u_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) of functions integrable on Q: if for every ε > 0 there are reals B, Λ and functions w_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) with |w_k(x)| ≤ B for x ∈ Q, |w_k(x) − w_k(y)| ≤ Λ‖x − y‖ for x, y ∈ Q, and ∫⁻_Q ‖u_k − w_k‖ₑ ≤ ofReal ε for every k, then for every ε > 0 there is a finite set F ⊆ ℕ such that every k ∈ ℕ has some j ∈ F with ∫⁻_Q ‖u_k(x) − u_j(x)‖ₑ dx < ofReal ε.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, Theorem 2.6 (p. 50). The printed proof reduces compactness to precompactness in L¹_loc(U), proved “involving mollification and Arzela's theorem” [GT01, Thm 7.22]; this step is the Arzelà-type finite-net argument. The argument below is step A1(iii)–(iv) of the reviewed proof supplied to node root.bv_results-a1.compactness-a1 (Section A of the parent root.bv_results-a1), specialized to this self-contained statement with the details filled in. Notation: ℝⁿ = Rn n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μ = volume (Lebesgue measure), ∫⁻ is the lower Lebesgue integral in [0,∞], ‖a‖ₑ ∈ [0,∞) the extended norm, ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal.

Statement recalled. Q ⊆ ℝⁿ is compact, every u_k is integrable on Q, and (approximation hypothesis) for every ε > 0 there are reals B, Λ and functions w_k (k ∈ ℕ) with |w_k(x)| ≤ B (x ∈ Q), |w_k(x) − w_k(y)| ≤ Λ‖x − y‖ (x, y ∈ Q) and ∫⁻_Q ‖u_k − w_k‖ₑ ≤ ofReal ε for all k. Claim: for every ε > 0 there is a finite F ⊆ ℕ such that every k has some j ∈ F with ∫⁻_Q ‖u_k − u_j‖ₑ < ofReal ε.

1. Fix ε > 0. Q is compact, hence closed, hence measurable, and μ(Q) < ∞ (IsCompact.measure_lt_top). Put m := μ(Q).toReal ≥ 0, so μ(Q) = ofReal m.

2. If Q = ∅, take F := {0}: for every k, ∫⁻_∅ ‖u_k − u_0‖ₑ = 0 < ofReal ε (μ.restrict ∅ = 0, ε > 0). Assume from now on Q ≠ ∅.

3. Apply the approximation hypothesis with ε/4 > 0 to get B, Λ and (w_k). Put Λ' := max(Λ, 0) ≥ 0; then |w_k(x) − w_k(y)| ≤ Λ‖x − y‖ ≤ Λ'‖x − y‖ for x, y ∈ Q.

4. Put η := ε / (4(m + 1)) > 0 and r := η / (3Λ' + 3) > 0. Since Q is compact there is a finite set T ⊆ Q with Q ⊆ ⋃_{q ∈ T} B(q, r) (open balls; finite_cover_balls_of_compact).

5. Rounding to a grid of spacing η/3. For k ∈ ℕ and q ∈ T let a_k(q) := round(3 w_k(q)/η) ∈ ℤ. By abs_sub_round, |3w_k(q)/η − a_k(q)| ≤ 1/2, i.e. |w_k(q) − (η/3) a_k(q)| ≤ η/6. Moreover |a_k(q)| ≤ 3|w_k(q)|/η + 1/2 ≤ 3B/η + 1 =: N, because q ∈ Q gives |w_k(q)| ≤ B. Hence every a_k lies in the set 𝒜 of functions T → {z ∈ ℤ : |z| ≤ N}, which is finite (T is finite and there are finitely many integers in [−N, N]).

6. Representatives. The set {a_k : k ∈ ℕ} ⊆ 𝒜 is finite. For each a in it choose an index j(a) ∈ ℕ with a_{j(a)} = a (for instance the least such index). Let F be the finite set {j(a) : a ∈ {a_k : k ∈ ℕ}} ⊆ ℕ (a Finset).

7. Fix k ∈ ℕ and put j := j(a_k) ∈ F, so a_j = a_k. For q ∈ T: |w_k(q) − w_j(q)| ≤ |w_k(q) − (η/3)a_k(q)| + |(η/3)a_j(q) − w_j(q)| ≤ η/6 + η/6 = η/3.

8. Let x ∈ Q and choose q ∈ T with ‖x − q‖ < r (step 4). Since x, q ∈ Q,
   |w_k(x) − w_j(x)| ≤ |w_k(x) − w_k(q)| + |w_k(q) − w_j(q)| + |w_j(q) − w_j(x)| ≤ Λ'r + η/3 + Λ'r = 2Λ'η/(3Λ' + 3) + η/3 < 2η/3 + η/3 = η,
   because 2Λ'/(3Λ' + 3) < 2/3 (equivalently 6Λ' < 6Λ' + 6). So ‖w_k(x) − w_j(x)‖ₑ ≤ ofReal η for all x ∈ Q.

9. Integrating over Q (setLIntegral_mono / ae_restrict_of_forall_mem, Q measurable): ∫⁻_Q ‖w_k − w_j‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_Q ofReal η = ofReal η · μ(Q) = ofReal(η m) ≤ ofReal(ε/4), since η m = ε m / (4(m + 1)) ≤ ε/4.

10. Measurability. u_k and u_j are a.e.-strongly measurable for μ.restrict Q (they are integrable on Q). Each w_i is Lipschitz on Q (step 3), hence continuous on Q, hence a.e.-strongly measurable for μ.restrict Q (ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable, Q measurable). Therefore x ↦ ‖u_k(x) − w_k(x)‖ₑ and x ↦ ‖w_k(x) − w_j(x)‖ₑ are a.e.-measurable for μ.restrict Q.

11. Triangle inequality. For every x, ‖u_k(x) − u_j(x)‖ₑ ≤ ‖u_k(x) − w_k(x)‖ₑ + ‖w_k(x) − w_j(x)‖ₑ + ‖w_j(x) − u_j(x)‖ₑ (write u_k − u_j = (u_k − w_k) + (w_k − w_j) + (w_j − u_j) and apply enorm_add_le twice; equivalently edist_triangle twice). By monotonicity of ∫⁻, additivity when the left summand is a.e.-measurable (lintegral_add_left', twice, using step 10), ‖w_j − u_j‖ₑ = ‖u_j − w_j‖ₑ, the approximation hypothesis (for k and for j) and step 9:
   ∫⁻_Q ‖u_k − u_j‖ₑ ≤ ofReal(ε/4) + ofReal(ε/4) + ofReal(ε/4) = ofReal(3ε/4) < ofReal ε (as ε > 0).

12. Since k was arbitrary and j ∈ F, the finite set F has the required property. ∎

Remark (equivalent shortcut for steps 5–8, convenient in Lean). Instead of rounding, view p_k := (w_k(q))_{q ∈ T} as a point of the finite-dimensional space T → ℝ with the sup norm. All p_k lie in the closed ball of radius max(B, 0), which is compact, so {p_k : k ∈ ℕ} is totally bounded and has a finite η/2-net consisting of points of the set (Metric.finite_approx_of_totallyBounded); choosing one index j for each net point (e.g. Function.invFun) gives F with ‖p_k − p_j‖ < η/2 for some j ∈ F. Taking r := η/(4(Λ' + 1)) in step 4, step 8 becomes |w_k(x) − w_j(x)| ≤ 2Λ'r + η/2 = Λ'η/(2(Λ' + 1)) + η/2 < η, and steps 9–12 are unchanged.

η := ε/(4(Lⁿ(Q).toReal + 1)); finite r-net T ⊆ Q of the compact Q with r := η/(3Λ' + 3).
Round w_k(q), q ∈ T, to the grid (η/3)ℤ: the codes a_k : T → [−N, N] ∩ ℤ take finitely many values; F := one index per code.
Equal codes give |w_k − w_j| ≤ η/3 on T and |w_k − w_j| < η on Q, so ∫⁻_Q‖w_k − w_j‖ₑ ≤ ofReal(ε/4).
Triangle inequality with a.e.-measurable summands: ∫⁻_Q‖u_k − u_j‖ₑ ≤ ofReal(3ε/4) < ofReal ε.

subproblem.title: Unweighted uniform L¹ and variation bounds from the frozen weighted hypothesis (step A0)
subproblem.statement: For every n ∈ ℕ, every open W ⊆ ℝⁿ (ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) with Lⁿ(W) < ∞, and every sequence u_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) such that sup_k ∫⁻_W (‖u_k(x)‖ₑ + |Du_k|(W)) dx < ∞ in [0,∞], where |Du_k|(W) := SimonGMT Chapter02.bvVariationOn (u k) W ∈ [0,∞] is an x-independent constant inside the integrand, there is a real c ≥ 0 such that for every k: ∫⁻_W ‖u_k(x)‖ₑ dx ≤ ofReal c and |Du_k|(W) ≤ ofReal c.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (W : Set (Rn n)) (u : ℕ → Rn n → ℝ), IsOpen W → volume W < ⊤ → ⨆ k, (∫⁻ x in W, ‖u k x‖ₑ + Chapter02.bvVariationOn (u k) W) < ⊤ → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 ≤ c ∧ ∀ k, (∫⁻ x in W, ‖u k x‖ₑ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal c ∧ Chapter02.bvVariationOn (u k) W ≤ ENNReal.ofReal c
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, Theorem 2.6 (p. 50). The printed hypothesis is sup_k (‖u_k‖_{L¹(W)} + ∫_W |Du_k|) < ∞ for W ⊂⊂ U; the frozen contract places the constant |Du_k|(W) inside the integrand, and this step recovers the printed unweighted bound. The argument below is step A0 of the reviewed proof supplied to node root.bv_results-a1.compactness-a1 (Section A of the parent root.bv_results-a1), specialized to this self-contained statement with the details filled in. Notation: ℝⁿ = Rn n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μ = volume (Lebesgue measure), ∫⁻ is the lower Lebesgue integral in [0,∞], ‖a‖ₑ ∈ [0,∞) the extended norm, ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal.

Statement recalled. W ⊆ ℝⁿ is open with μ(W) < ∞, u_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ), b_k := Chapter02.bvVariationOn (u k) W ∈ [0,∞] (an x-independent constant), and S := ⨆_k ∫⁻_W (‖u_k(x)‖ₑ + b_k) dx < ∞ (the whole sum is the integrand). We must find a real c ≥ 0 with ∫⁻_W ‖u_k‖ₑ ≤ ofReal c and b_k ≤ ofReal c for every k.

1. Case W = ∅. Take c := 0 (so ofReal c = 0). For each k, ∫⁻_∅ ‖u_k‖ₑ = 0 because μ.restrict ∅ = 0 (Measure.restrict_empty). Also b_k = 0: by definition b_k is the supremum, over compactly supported Lipschitz fields g with tsupport g ⊆ ∅ and sup-norm ≤ 1, of ofReal(∫_∅ u_k · div g dx); every such Bochner integral is taken against the zero measure μ.restrict ∅ = 0, hence equals 0, and ofReal 0 = 0; a supremum of zeros (or an empty supremum) in [0,∞] is 0. (In Lean: simp [Chapter02.bvVariationOn].) Both required bounds hold.

2. Case W ≠ ∅. Then 0 < μ(W): W is open and nonempty and Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ is an additive Haar measure, hence positive on nonempty open sets (IsOpen.measure_pos; for n = 0 the space is a single point of measure 1). And μ(W) < ∞ by hypothesis. So μ(W) ≠ 0 and μ(W) ≠ ∞.

3. Fix k. The function x ↦ b_k is constant, hence measurable, so by lintegral_add_right and setLIntegral_const
   ∫⁻_W (‖u_k(x)‖ₑ + b_k) dx = ∫⁻_W ‖u_k‖ₑ + b_k · μ(W).
   This quantity is one of the terms of the supremum S, so (le_iSup) ∫⁻_W ‖u_k‖ₑ + b_k · μ(W) ≤ S.

4. From step 3 (both summands are ≤ their sum in [0,∞]): ∫⁻_W ‖u_k‖ₑ ≤ S and b_k · μ(W) ≤ S. Since μ(W) ≠ 0 and μ(W) ≠ ∞, ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le turns the second inequality into b_k ≤ S / μ(W).

5. Put C := S + S/μ(W) ∈ [0,∞]. C < ∞: S < ∞ by hypothesis and S/μ(W) < ∞ by ENNReal.div_lt_top (S ≠ ∞, μ(W) ≠ 0). Let c := C.toReal ≥ 0; since C ≠ ∞, ofReal c = C (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal).

6. For every k: ∫⁻_W ‖u_k‖ₑ ≤ S ≤ S + S/μ(W) = ofReal c and b_k ≤ S/μ(W) ≤ S + S/μ(W) = ofReal c (steps 4 and 5). Together with c ≥ 0 this is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: W = ∅: both integrals vanish (μ.restrict ∅ = 0), and bvVariationOn _ ∅ = 0 since every term of its supremum is ofReal 0; take c = 0.
W ≠ ∅: 0 < Lⁿ(W) < ∞ (open nonempty set for a Haar measure; hypothesis).
lintegral_add_right + setLIntegral_const: ∫⁻_W(‖u_k‖ₑ + b_k) = ∫⁻_W‖u_k‖ₑ + b_k·Lⁿ(W) ≤ S.
ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le: b_k ≤ S/Lⁿ(W); C := S + S/Lⁿ(W) < ∞.
c := C.toReal ≥ 0 with ofReal c = C bounds both quantities for every k.
